key_insight: CFD-driven symbolic regression learns compact, interpretable corrections to a RANS transition model that improve predictions beyond the flat-plate training cases.
engineering_relevance: More accurate transition modeling can improve turbomachinery heat-transfer and loss predictions, with heat-transfer errors reduced by up to 70% in tested turbine-cascade conditions.
method: Correct intermittency production and destruction activation functions using pressure-gradient polynomials and bounded exponentials of local flow features.
Fit coefficients with gradient-free, RANS-in-the-loop optimization accelerated by POD-Kriging field surrogates.
Select elastic-net hyperparameters through bi-level optimization and leave-one-case-out cross-validation.
evidence_signal: Trained on wall-resolved LES mean velocities for ERCOFTAC T3 flat plates, the model retained 11 of 21 candidate terms and improved heat-transfer predictions at all four unseen LS89 turbine-cascade operating points without retraining.
watch_item: Residual errors in transition onset and length indicate that flat-plate-only training limits predictive accuracy in more complex flows.
paper_title: CFD-driven symbolic regression of RANS transition models
